thread:
natalie: Quick sync — SOC asked earlier: who is allowed to request SIEM exports older than 30d and what's the KMS unwrap/JIT access flow? Need a short playbook + ticket template by EOD Friday.

raj: Clarify scope — forensic investigations only, or analytics/partner deliveries too?

natalie: Forensics initially. Partners/analytics will follow a separate process. Forensics exports could be up to 180 days, timeboxed, JIT unwrap, full audit trail.

emma: Proposed RBAC model: create role `security:siem_exporter` with ability to `request_export` only. `view_unwrapped` should NOT be granted by default — only via ephemeral grant (JIT) after approval. Approval chain: Requestor -> Oncall Sec -> CISO delegate for >72h access.

emma: Draft ticket template (put this into the ops ticket):
```
- requestor: <email>
- case_id: <INC|CASE|INV-####>
- justification: <why export is needed>
- time_range: <start,end>
- retention_days: <how long exported snapshots persist, e.g. 14>
- kms_key: <logs-cmk-id>
- scrub_required: <yes/no>
- recipients: <aws-account/principal>
- expiry_ts: <UTC timestamp when access should auto-revoke>
- approvers: <oncall_sec, sec_mgr>
- audit_link: <link to ticket/audit log>
```

raj: KMS unwrap/ephemeral grant details: use the KMUX proxy and ephemeral grants service. Approvals should call `gms-grant` to create a short-lived unwrap token. Example: `gms-grant --principal=security:siem_exporter --key=logs-cmk --ttl=2h --reason="forensics CASE-1287"` — token is logged to audit-bus, and unwrap attempts require that token header.

ops-bot: audit:export_requested case=CASE-1287 by=natalie

emma: Storage: exports must land in a temp S3 bucket with SSE-KMS using the same CMK, bucket-level policy to deny public access, and a lifecycle rule to delete after `retention_days`. Bucket access restricted to `siem_exporter` ephemeral role only.

matt: Add vuln-triage note: if the export includes PII or sensitive indicators, DLP must run before delivery. If DLP flags, scrub and re-review in the same ticket. Link to DLP playbook: https://redwood.internal/dlp/playbook

security-analyst: +1 on DLP. Who runs the scrub pipeline in practice — SOC or data-platform?

raj: SOC performs initial manual review/scrub for high-severity incidents. For routine exports, data-platform owns automated redact pipeline (regex-based + allowlist). We should add a checklist entry in the ticket for which path to use.

emma: Breakglass / incident flow: allow emergency unwrap with two-person authorization (requestor + oncall sec OR product incident lead) but still require a retroactive CISO review within 24h. All breakglass unwraps must trigger CMK rotation audit flag if used more than once for same case.

taylor: Operational detail — ephemeral bucket TTLs: default export snapshot retention = 14 days, ephemeral access TTL = 2 hours, review window = 72 hours to decide extension. If extension needed, escalate to CISO delegate.

emma: Security controls summary to include in playbook: RBAC role, ticket template, KMS ephemeral grant flow, ephemeral bucket config, DLP hook, audit log retention for unwrap tokens (retain 1 year), and post-export rotation guidance.

natalie: Action items: emma will draft the playbook + ticket template and post PR to infra-playbooks. taylor will provision a templated bucket and lifecycle rules. raj to review KMS policy and supply `gms-grant` env examples. matt will update DLP checklist. Deadline: Friday COB.

ops-bot: reminder set: playbook-draft-review @emma @taylor @raj @matt due=1735630800

natalie: Thanks everyone — if you're blocked ping me or drop the draft in #eng-security for quick review. :thumbsup:
